title: North Korean Missile Unit Deploys to Russia With Up to 120 Ballistic Missiles for Ukraine Strikes
excerpt: Ukrainian intelligence says about 90 North Korean personnel are setting up in Russia's Voronezh region, days after a Pyongyang-made missile killed five members of a Ukrainian family.
body:
• A North Korean missile unit of about 90 personnel has begun deploying to Russia's Voronezh region, potentially equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers, according to Ukrainian military intelligence.
  • The deployment follows a deadly North Korean missile strike on the Ukrainian village of Radushne that killed at least five members of a single family — the first use of North Korean missiles in Ukraine since August 2025.
  • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned in July that Russia wants to bring in 30,000 additional North Korean troops, with preparations already underway in the Voronezh region.
  • Around 9,500 North Korean troops remain in Russia's Kursk region from a 2024 deployment, though they are not currently directly involved in operations against Ukraine.

A North Korean missile unit has begun deploying to western Russia and could be equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers for strikes against Ukraine, a Ukrainian military intelligence official said, marking a significant escalation of Pyongyang's involvement in Europe's largest conflict since World War II.

The disclosure came days after a North Korean ballistic missile flattened a residential home in the central Ukrainian village of Radushne, killing at least five members of the Voronov family — the first confirmed use of North Korean missiles in Ukraine since August 2025.

What We Know About the Deployment

Andrii Cherniak of Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence told Reuters that Russia planned to base the missile unit of approximately 90 North Korean personnel within its 112th Missile Brigade in the Voronezh region. Pyongyang has already shipped a batch of 40 KN-23 and KN-24 missiles along with personnel, but the full configuration — expected to include 120 missiles and six launchers — will be finalized in top-level talks next month.

https://x.com/clashreport/status/2086158662523932978

A source familiar with the issue confirmed to Reuters that the United States is aware of the deployment. The CIA declined to comment, and the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

"Ballistic missile defence is one of Ukraine's greatest vulnerabilities so any increase in the quantities of ballistic missiles they face will pose a greater challenge."

— Rob Lee, Senior Fellow, Foreign Policy Research Institute

A Family Destroyed by a North Korean Missile

The urgency of the missile threat was underscored last week when a ballistic missile crashed through the roof of the Voronov family home in Radushne, a small village outside Kryvyi Rih — President Zelenskyy's hometown. The family had lived there with seven of their ten children.

"The most terrible thing was the silence," neighbor Lyudmyla Yosypovych told The Times. "We knew then that no one had survived."

In his nightly address, Zelenskyy confirmed the missile was North Korean: "The alliance between the Moscow scumbags and the deranged regime in North Korea exists for the sake of missiles, North Korean troops on our borders here in Europe and killing our Ukrainian children."

Bigger Warheads, Less Accuracy

North Korea's KN-23 and KN-24 missiles have a greater range and larger payload than Russia's equivalent Iskander system, but they are significantly less accurate, according to Ukrainian military sources. This imprecision has been linked to strikes with disproportionately high civilian death tolls.

Russia has fired scores of North Korean ballistic missiles at Ukraine since late 2023. Cherniak said North Korea supplied 150 of the missiles between the end of 2023 and August 2025, and that the new batch of 40 represents a fresh supply line.

30,000 More Troops on the Horizon

The missile deployment comes alongside warnings of a much larger force buildup. In late July, Zelenskyy said Russia wanted to bring in 30,000 additional North Korean troops, with preparations underway in the Voronezh region since June. Japan's NHK News separately reported that a Russian diplomatic source confirmed Putin and North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui had discussed a deployment of around 20,000 troops.

Around 9,500 North Korean troops from a 2024 deployment remain in Russia's Kursk region, though Ukrainian intelligence said they are not currently directly involved in military operations. North Korea originally sent 14,000 to 15,000 soldiers to help Moscow repel a Ukrainian ground incursion into Kursk.

What's at Stake This Winter

Rob Lee, a senior fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute, warned that a particularly big concern for Ukraine will be the state of its air defenses this winter, when Russia could again target the power grid with heavy attacks as it did in previous years. The addition of North Korean ballistic missiles — which can only be intercepted by U.S.-made Patriot air defense systems — would stretch Ukraine's already thin missile shield further.

NATO has said Russia's growing military ties with North Korea, China, and Iran pose a threat extending beyond Europe to the Indo-Pacific and North America. The question for Kyiv and its Western allies is whether enough interceptors will be available when the next major wave arrives.
